Override animations for a mobject class

Source: R/animation.R
override_animation.Rd

override_animation() makes an animation constructor build something else for one mobject class, like upstream's @override_animation decorator: after override_animation(MyMobClass, "FadeIn", function(...) ...), FadeIn(my_mob, ...) calls the function as a method of my_mob (so it can use self) with the remaining arguments, and returns its result. Pass use_override = FALSE to the constructor to get the normal animation. Only the package's constructor functions (such as FadeIn()) check for overrides, not FadeInClass$new().

Usage

override_animation(mobject_class, animation, fn)

override_animate(mobject_class, method, fn)

Arguments

mobject_class

A mobject class generator, such as SquareClass or your own R6 class.

animation

An animation class name, such as "FadeIn", or its generator (FadeInClass).

fn

The override function.

method

Name of the mobject method to customize under $animate.

Value

The class generator, invisibly.

Details

override_animate() customizes mob$animate$method(...), like upstream's @override_animate: the function is called as a method of the mobject with the method's arguments plus anim_args, the list of arguments given to animate (such as run_time), and returns an animation.

Both change the class generator in place (with $set()), so they apply to objects created afterwards, including objects of subclasses.

Examples

Pulse <- R6::R6Class("Pulse", inherit = CircleClass, lock_objects = FALSE)
override_animation(Pulse, "FadeIn", function(...) GrowFromCenter(self, ...))
class(FadeIn(Pulse$new()))[1]
#> [1] "GrowFromCenter"
